# Load the dataset

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a new column to categorize the cameras by price range
bins = [0, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 10000]
labels = ['<500', '500-1000', '1000-2000', '2000-3000', '3000-4000', '4000-5000', '5000+']
data['price_range'] = pd.cut(data['price_usd'], bins=bins, labels=labels)

# Create a bar plot to visualize the count of cameras in each price range and sensor type
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.countplot(data=data, x='price_range', hue='sensor_type', palette="viridis")

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Prices by Sensor Type', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Price Range (USD)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=12)
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type')

# Save the plot to a file
